transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-14 16:30 PT / Duration: ~55m / Attendees: Evan, Marisol, Rohit (Redwood) - Samantha, Jared, Aisha, Tom (Opal)

[00:00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today, we'll run through the audit log and admin activity capture, talk through export options, and KMS. Quick intro round?
[00:00:10] Samantha: Hi I'm Samantha, head of security at Opal. We're primarily focused on retention, proof of admin actions, and ensuring we can ingest logs into our SIEM.
[00:00:18] Jared: Jared, platform, curious about event granularity and how names/tokens are surfaced. Also residency questions.
[00:00:24] Aisha: Legal here, short on time but want to confirm encryption and legal hold.
[00:00:30] Evan: Great. Marisol will walk through event types and export. Marisol?
[00:00:34] Marisol: Sure. High level — Redwood captures three broad classes: API-level call events (who called what model, request metadata, success/fail, tokens), console/admin events (user role changes, RBAC updates, SSO mappings, key rotations, rollout changes), and system-level infra events (autoscale actions, node replacements - less common for customers but we log). We also tag events with request_id, user_id, and account_id.
[00:01:05] Tom: When you say user_id, is that the raw username or an internal id? We need pseudonymized data in logs for GDPR.
[00:01:12] Marisol: By default we include an internal user_id and a username display field. For GDPR you can request pseudonymization or suppression of PII in exports; we support both masking patterns and tokenization. It's a configuration at export time — can be per-bucket or per-export job.
[00:01:32] Jared: What about token-level detail? We don't want the entire prompt or PII to be in logs.
[00:01:38] Marisol: We don't dump full request bodies in standard admin logs. We capture request metadata (model, latency, token counts, status) and a hashed request fingerprint. If a customer enables full request auditing (for debugging) that is opt-in and flagged as high-sensitivity — recommended only for short retention.
[00:01:58] Samantha: Can you enumerate specific admin actions captured?
[00:02:02] Marisol: Sure — user create/delete, role change, SAML/SSO mapping changes, API key create/revoke/rotate, KMS key link/unlink, model pin/rollout changes, policy updates, and export actions. We also log permission denials and failed auth attempts.
[00:02:20] Evan: Important to note, each event has a change diff payload when applicable — e.g., role change shows before/after role names — again subject to masking rules.
[00:02:31] Aisha: For legal holds, if we need to keep an event longer, is there a way to mark it?
[00:02:36] Marisol: Yes, Redwood supports per-account legal hold flags. When activated, retention enforcement is suspended for that account's export bucket and logs are preserved until the hold is removed. We track hold create/delete as audit events.
[00:02:48] Tom: Export destinations? We want streaming into our Kafka cluster but also a cold store in GCS.
[00:02:54] Marisol: Exports supported today: native S3/GCS delivery (batch/rolling files), streaming via Kafka, HTTP webhook streaming (deliver SSE/POST batches), and direct SIEM connectors (we've done Splunk/Datadog customers). For Kafka we can deliver avro or newline-delimited JSON; for S3/GCS we emit gzipped JSONL with partitioning by date and account.
[00:03:16] Jared: If we use Kafka, can we choose schema evolution path? Avro + schema registry?
[00:03:21] Marisol: Yes, we support Avro with Confluent schema registry or a simple JSON schema; we can version schemas and include schema_id in each message.
[00:03:29] Samantha: How long do you keep logs on Redwood by default?
[00:03:33] Marisol: Default retention for admin/audit logs in the control plane is 90 days. Hosted customers with retention add-on can extend to 1 year, 3 years, or custom windows. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers typically manage their own retention.
[00:03:47] Aisha: We need five years for some records per regulations. Is that supported?
[00:03:51] Marisol: For hosted API, yes via the long-term retention add-on — we can retain in our infra but it's common to export to your cold store (GCS) for 5+ years. We can also enable read-only snapshots for compliance review. If you require immutable storage we recommend using customer-controlled GCS/S3 with Object Lock (WORM) + customer KMS.
[00:04:10] Tom: About KMS — can we bring our own KMS/HSM keys?
[00:04:13] Marisol: Yes. We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and also integrate with HSMs via CloudHSM or customer HSM for Private deployments. Keys can be used to encrypt exported logs and also to wrap internal storage keys if needed.
[00:04:26] Jared: Are export objects encrypted with customer key or your key?
[00:04:30] Marisol: We support both. You can choose server-side encryption with Redwood-managed keys, or SSE-C/SSE-KMS with your CMK for S3; for GCS you can provide customer-managed encryption keys. For streaming exports we encrypt at rest on our side and use TLS in transit; we can also encrypt payloads with your public key before sending if required.
[00:04:48] Samantha: Data residency — can logs generated in EU be kept in EU?
[00:04:52] Marisol: Yes. Exports can be region-bound; we can configure export runners in EU regions so logs never leave region. For hosted we offer region selection per account, and Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[00:05:02] Aisha: About access controls — who in Redwood can see raw audit logs?
[00:05:06] Marisol: Access to raw audit logs is restricted to a small set of infra ops engineers under strict least-privilege and audited ourselves. For customers, RBAC allows you to scope which roles can view exports via console or API. We have SSO+SCIM + role mapping so you can centrally control.
[00:05:21] Evan: We also support token-level billing visibility without exposing content; you can get token counts per user without the prompt text.
[00:05:28] Tom: On schema: will you share a sample event?
[00:05:31] Marisol: Yes I'll share schema. Example event: {"timestamp":"...","event_type":"admin.role.change","actor_id":"u-123","account_id":"acct-789","resource":"role/engineer","change":{"before":"viewer","after":"editor"},"request_id":"r-456","region":"eu-west-1"} — although actual export is JSONL gzipped.
[00:05:48] Jared: Any rate limits on exports? We have bursty admin activity during deploys.
[00:05:52] Marisol: For batch S3/GCS it's mostly throughput limited by object size; for streaming Kafka/webhook we impose per-account concurrency limits to avoid thundering herd — we can increase for Dedicated or with negotiated SLAs.
[00:06:04] Samantha: Audit integrity — can we verify logs haven't been tampered with?
[00:06:09] Marisol: We can offer signed manifests and SHA256 checksums for each blob. For high assurance setups we can produce append-only chains with signatures (similar to ledger approach) — usually part of an enterprise compliance package.
[00:06:22] Aisha: Do you provide retention deletion proofs for GDPR right to be forgotten?
[00:06:28] Marisol: Yes, we can produce deletion receipts and record the deletion event in an audit trail. For exported copies on your side, deletion is your responsibility unless you use Redwood-managed cold store.
[00:06:37] Tom: Is there an API to trigger on-demand exports?
[00:06:40] Marisol: Yes, there's an exports API to run ad-hoc jobs with filters (time window, event types, accounts). We also have scheduled exports.
[00:06:47] Jared: For SIEM, can you push enriched events (with geo, user-role) or do we get raw?
[00:06:52] Marisol: We support both raw and enriched. Enrichment is configurable (adds role, department, resolved user email) but again PII controls apply.
[00:07:02] Samantha: What's in the default admin console audit view?
[00:07:05] Evan: The console shows recent admin actions, quick filters, and a download button. For deep forensic work we recommend exports to your SIEM.
[00:07:12] Samantha: Any known gaps / non-captured events?
[00:07:15] Marisol: We don't currently capture low-level kernel events from the infra nodes (not relevant to customers) and ephemeral internal debug logs are excluded. We capture all customer-facing control plane events. There can be small delays (seconds to low minutes) for delivery depending on pipeline.
[00:07:30] Tom: Could you support immutable WORM exports on S3?
[00:07:33] Marisol: Yes — if you use your S3 with Object Lock and we write to that bucket, you get WORM semantics. We can also set retention metadata.
[00:07:42] Aisha: If we request longer retention inside Redwood, is there a cost impact?
[00:07:46] Evan: Yes typical pricing is monthly per GB for retained logs plus surcharge for immutable/legal hold features. We'll include pricing in follow-up.
[00:07:56] Samantha: For discovery, what would the pilot look like?
[00:07:59] Rohit: We can enable a 2-week export to your Kafka topic and provide schema + connectors, and an ops runbook. After that we can discuss long-term retention and contractual terms.
[00:08:10] Jared: Timeline for the docs?
[00:08:12] Evan: We'll send SOC2 and sample schema by Monday (2025-02-17). Marisol will spin up the sandbox export by 2025-02-20.
[00:08:20] Samantha: A quick note — we need evidence of role-based access within Redwood for specific users when we audit.
[00:08:27] Marisol: We'll include a section showing RBAC mappings and where to find audit trails for RBAC itself.
[00:08:34] Aisha: Legal asks for a copy of the KMS key lifecycle policy.
[00:08:38] Marisol: We'll include KMS lifecycle docs and HSM integration notes.
[00:08:43] Evan: Any other questions?
[00:08:45] Samantha: One last one — do you keep a timeline of admin actions for model rollouts? We need to prove who approved model changes.
[00:08:51] Marisol: Absolutely — rollout events include approver id, timestamp, and rollout percentage with diffs. Those are part of the admin audit log.
[00:08:59] Tom: Ok that covers most. We'll review docs and get back on pilot.
[00:09:03] Evan: Thanks everyone, recap and next steps in email.

[00:09:10] --- end of recorded transcript excerpt (the call continued with scheduling details and minor clarifications)
